title: Field-level consistency verifier and calibration loop for FP8/INT8 structured outputs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a post-quantization verification and automated calibration loop that measures per-field JSON schema adherence and numeric fidelity for function-call outputs. This ticket introduces a Field-level Consistency Score (FCS) and a Schema Token Alignment (STA) metric to quantify structural and token-level regressions caused by FP8/INT8 quantization profiles. The verifier will run as part of stage and canary pipelines and trigger calibration replays or fallback routing when thresholds are violated.
acceptance_criteria: FCS and STA metrics are implemented and emitted per-request in the test harness (quant-field-replay)
A baseline calibration job can be launched for a given model+quant-profile that produces a calibration artifact and expected FCS/STA baselines
Automated CI check fails if FCS < 0.995 or STA < 0.98 for production-critical prompt sets
Console dashboard shows per-model, per-profile FCS and a breakdown by JSON field (missing, type-mismatch, value-truncation)
Canary policy defined: if weekly production FCS drops by >0.5% for any customer route, automatically route to higher-precision variant and open incident ticket
implementation_plan: Design metric definitions and per-field tolerances (doc: confluence/quant/field-consistency)
Extend existing structured-output harness to produce per-field diffs and token-alignment traces (new harness: quant-field-replay)
Add lightweight instrumentation to runtime to emit schema-violation events (sinks: metrics, audit log)
Create calibration workflow hook that iteratively adjusts quant profiles and re-evaluates FCS/STA until thresholds met or budget exhausted
Add CI gate: run verifier against nightly calibration artifacts for FP8 and INT8 variants
Expose results in Redwood Console and add alerting rules (SLO burn, regression alert)
Ship rollback/fallback routing policy for failing routes
test_plan: Seed testbench with 5K representative function-call prompts covering nested objects, optional fields, arrays, and edge-case strings
Introduce adversarial mutation set (truncation, extra keys, swapped types) to verify detector sensitivity
Compare outputs from fp32 vs FP8 vs INT8 profiles using quant-field-replay and compute FCS/STA distributions
Run end-to-end canary: deploy FP8 profile to 5% of traffic and validate FCS stability over 48h
Add regression tests to CI: new failures block PRs for runtime/quant modules
rollout_plan: Stage rollout: enable verifier and metrics in staging, run 72h smoke with representative traffic
Canary rollout: 5% production with auto-monitoring; if FCS < threshold for 10m window, trigger immediate rollback to previous profile
Gradual expansion to 25% then 100% depending on observed stability and cost impact
Operational playbook: how to interpret per-field failures and when to request re-calibration vs route to higher precision
decisions: Metric choice: FCS (structural) + STA (token alignment) chosen to separate structural schema issues from subtle tokenization drift
Thresholds: initial gating set conservatively (FCS 0.995, STA 0.98) and will be tuned after two calibration iterations
Enforcement: production CI gates will be enabled for release branches touching runtime or model onboarding
Fallback: prefer routing to compatible model variant (quant profile with slightly higher precision) rather than rejecting requests
tradeoffs: Tighter thresholds reduce risk of customer-visible regressions but increase calibration compute costs and CI runtime
Per-field fine-grain checks provide better diagnostics but add cardinality to metrics and dashboard complexity
Automated re-calibration can increase latency to ship model variants; tradeoff mitigated by asynchronous calibration and canary routing
